claims.claim: Reachability is exactly a sparse unary congruence-closure query.
claims.evidence: Let θ be the least equivalence satisfying the stated folding rule. A bottom-stack path returning to the bottom is a well-nested push/pop word. Decomposing it into concatenations and outermost push-X/balanced/pop-X segments proves inductively that its endpoints are θ-equivalent. Conversely, each folding step is realized by pushing X along one cited edge, following the already-certified stack-neutral path between targets, and popping X along the reverse of the other edge. Thus θ is exactly bottom-stack-neutral reachability. The DPDA exits precisely after reaching an outer-pin wire with the bottom symbol still present, so exitability is exactly whether the start is θ-equivalent to such a wire. For each X, the quotient relation [t]↦[o] is a well-defined partial unary map; pin names add no constraint after edge endpoints and accepting wires are fixed.
claims.search_method: Independent structural induction on legal push/pop paths, followed by exhaustive comparison with explicit configuration reachability on all 512 one-box edge subsets over three wires.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic O(B+(W+E) log(W+E))-time, O(W+E+B)-space algorithm, eliminating the dense W·B initialization.
claims.evidence: A target-class map needs only one representative edge per box. Every key collision occurs between same-box edges whose targets are already equivalent, so its queued origin merge is forced. Discarded edges remain represented because their origins are queued and ultimately proved equivalent to the retained origin. When the queue empties, every original pair with the same box and equivalent targets has equivalent origins; hence the partition is stable. Since every performed merge was forced, it is the least stable partition. Each collision deletes one live edge entry, giving at most E queue events. Initial bounded-integer sorting costs O(W+E+B). Smaller-to-larger member relabeling costs O(W log W). A deterministic split/join balanced-tree meld of sizes m≤n costs O(m log(n/m+1)); overlap work is charged to entries deleted once, while non-overlap work is charged to the multiplicative growth of surviving entries, giving O(E log(E+1)) total. All lists, trees, edges, and queue records occupy O(W+E+B) space.
claims.search_method: Invariant and amortized-analysis audit, plus exhaustive comparison of the event-driven map algorithm against an independently implemented naive least fixed point on all 262,144 two-box edge subsets over three wires.

claims.claim: Both outcomes have certificates of size O(W+E) verifiable deterministically in O(W+E+B) time.
claims.evidence: For a negative certificate, equality of class numbers defines an equivalence P. Grouping edges by (X,P(t)) and requiring a unique P(o) per group verifies stability. The least closure refines every stable P, so separation in P proves nonreachability; the least closure supplies a certificate whenever the answer is negative. Bounded class identifiers permit deterministic two-pass radix sorting in O(W+E+B). For a positive certificate, chronological child indices and unique parent links define a binary merge forest with at most W−1 internal nodes. At each internal node, same-box source edges, origins in the respective child subtrees, and targets below an earlier node q soundly justify the merge. DFS intervals verify all containment tests in constant time. Chronology makes the induction well-founded, and any successful folding sequence yields such a forest. The certificate and verifier storage are linear.
claims.search_method: Separate soundness and completeness proofs for both certificate types; exhaustive construction and interval verification of 495,933 positive fold nodes across 262,144 graphs; enumeration of every partition for all 512 one-box graphs, checking all 861 stable negative certificates.

claims.claim: The target O(W+E+B) bound holds for graded dual graphs: graphs admitting an integer rank ρ with ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 for every edge (o,X,t).
claims.evidence: Induction on folding steps shows equivalences never cross ranks. Consequently, final rank-r classes depend only on already-final rank-(r−1) classes: for each pair (X,class(t)), add a star among its rank-r origins and compute ordinary undirected connected components. No later rule can alter rank r because every rule producing rank-r equalities uses rank-(r−1) targets. Timestamp arrays of lengths B and W implement the sparse grouping, and adjacency-list DFS implements components, with every edge and wire processed O(1) times. If ρ is not supplied, the equations ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 can be assigned and checked by DFS in each weak component in O(W+E); componentwise normalization gives an O(W)-sized rank range. Total time and space are O(W+E+B).
claims.search_method: Rank induction and operation accounting, plus exhaustive comparison with naive closure on all 65,536 admissible two-box edge subsets for six vertices of ranks (0,0,1,1,2,2).

claims.claim: Repeated global fixed-point rescanning can require Θ(W) changing rounds even with one box and E=Θ(W).
claims.evidence: After r synchronous changing rounds, the construction has exactly the blocks {a_k,b_k} for k<r, with z and all higher-level vertices still separate. In the next round, only a_r and b_r have equivalent targets; targets belonging to distinct levels never become equivalent. Hence the instance has exactly n+1 changing rounds, W=2n+3, and E=2n+2. Conversely, any changing round reduces the number of equivalence classes, so no instance has more than W−1 changing rounds. The family therefore establishes Θ(W). Distinct pin labels can be assigned to all edges, so the one-box construction respects the dual-maze representation.
claims.search_method: Exact induction on round number and exhaustive execution of the family for every n from 0 through 128.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an unrestricted deterministic O(W+E+B)-time reachability algorithm. The draft explicitly says it did not obtain that algorithm: its unrestricted construction retains a logarithmic overhead, its certificates do not provide a linear-time certificate finder, and its linear algorithm applies only to graded dual graphs. Those results are nevertheless correct and material partial progress. The final writeup accurately labels the resolution partial and does not claim full target coverage, so claimed_resolution is ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
